title: I'm bringing Dark Souls combat to WoW Classic using Claude — early prototype Kopiera
author: jabegames

comments.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
comments.body:
Did you just downloaded retail and asked claude to decompile and port the assets into a new game or did you mod the actual wow game?
Where does the server comme from?

replies.author: jabegames
replies.body:
Neither, and there’s no server.

WoW Souls is a separate single-player program written from scratch in Rust on the Bevy engine. I didn’t mod the WoW client, and nothing was decompiled or ported out of a retail executable.

The game reads the data files from my own WoW 1.12.1 install (the old vanilla Data folder: maps, models, textures, animations). The loading and rendering code comes from benilla, an open-source 1.12 client by samwhosung (MIT/Apache-2.0), which I use unmodified as a library. Those file formats are well documented, so no client code was involved.

There’s no login, no network and no realm. benilla can connect to a server, but WoW Souls only uses its world and model loading. The kobold’s AI, the damage and the respawn all run locally in my own code.

A small extractor tool reads the animations and parameter data (stamina costs, damage multipliers, hit windows) from my own Dark Souls Remastered install. It retargets those animations onto the WoW character skeleton and writes a local cache. That cache is never committed or shared. The extractor and the game are separate programs.

It is possible to make it with a server, like how private servers does it. But for now I just want to explore making a single player game in world of warcaft :)
